original_test_intent: Verify that each selected power cable or harness follows the approved source-to-load route, preserves insulation, clearance, bend and strain controls, remains clear of hot/moving/sharp features and airflow paths, is fully seated at both ends, and restores the expected loads without new power or thermal faults after the approved plug cycle.
original_method: A qualified engineer traces the entire power path against the routing drawing, performs the authorized isolated connector cycle, restores all clips and service loops, and records the full route. The agent may collect mapped power and availability evidence only after physical restoration.
manual_activity: The engineer identifies the cable's source, loads and every routing checkpoint; isolates and verifies discharge; inspects insulation and contacts; evaluates bend, torsion, abrasion, strain, service slack and clearance; performs the approved disconnect/reconnect; and restores clips, separators and seating. Remote status cannot establish these spatial and material conditions.
required_inputs: Power-cable/harness FRU and source-to-load connector map
Approved routing drawing with channels, clips, separators, service loops and keep-outs
Cable-specific bend, clearance, temperature and strain criteria
Expected post-cycle source/rail/PSU, load availability and thermal observations
Qualified operator and full-route photographic checklist
safety_requirements: De-energize and verify discharge before disconnecting or rerouting unless the exact interface is explicitly approved for energized service.
Do not infer generic bend or temperature limits; use the selected harness specification and preserve required separation from sharp edges, hot surfaces and moving parts.
Maintain airflow, fan clearance and service travel and avoid pinching, chafing, torsion, conductor pull or unsupported connector load.
Verify source/load orientation and connector keying; do not cross-connect rails or defeat polarization/retention.
Stop on damaged insulation, exposed conductor, discoloration, heat/odor, connector damage, route interference, abnormal telemetry or unexpected load loss.
Do not reroute experimentally, repeat the cycle, re-energize for troubleshooting or clear event history after an anomaly.
agent_execution_scope: Build a source-to-load route checklist from approved electrical and mechanical drawings.
Collect read-only pre-action source/rail/PSU, load, thermal and event evidence without operating power controls.
After engineer confirmation of final routing and authorized energization, collect the same mapped evidence and raw event delta.
Check photo coverage of all route segments and report discrepancies without claiming physical acceptance.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact harness, route, energy isolation and physical cycle.
Inspect and document the full path and both endpoints, perform the isolated cycle and restore every retention/routing feature.
Verify safe final route/seating and authorize energization/post-check.
Apply mechanical, electrical and thermal criteria and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The manual-only marker is appropriate, but its generic status does not prove full-route compliance. Supporting telemetry must be mapped to the cable's actual source and loads.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use project-approved read-only PSU/rail/load/thermal collectors after the power-path map is confirmed. No command replaces route inspection, and no power control, stress or recovery action is added by default.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Attended Time 10 and Machine Time 0 remain unchanged. The source has no cable ID, route limits, cycle count, electrical ratings or commands.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a segment-by-segment route photo matrix tied to cable FRU, source/load endpoints, isolation evidence and mapped post-restoration power/thermal observations.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected chassis, harness, power architecture and populated loads.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record electrical/mechanical drawings, harness/chassis revision, service procedure and BMC/firmware versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable platform power-routing, harness and service documentation; no generic bend, clearance, temperature or current limit is asserted.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes complete route coverage, energy controls and source/load correlation auditable while preserving the physical cycle.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Full coverage requires every route segment, retention point and endpoint plus restored mapped loads. Telemetry-only or endpoint-only evidence omits routing hazards.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Harness/source/load map, route drawing, cable limits, isolation method and expected observations.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Hidden route sections may remain unverified, and normal telemetry does not rule out abrasion, thermal exposure or a marginal high-current contact.

project_override_considerations: The project may select a harness subset or accessible route segments. It must record hidden/excluded segments and unmapped loads as coverage delta; successful operation of those loads does not complete uninspected routing coverage.
expected_evidence: Harness FRU/label and source-to-load endpoint map
Full-route checklist and photographs covering clips, bends, keep-outs, clearances, insulation, service loops and both endpoints
Raw mapped pre/post power, load, fan/thermal and event evidence
Safety stops, inaccessible/excluded segments and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Procedure's physical cycle/detection and Criteria's seating requirement are consistent with Power Routing. Missing route values and topology are project inputs rather than contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The end-to-end routing and restoration intent is clear. The harness map, limits and isolation plan gate execution but do not permanently block review.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keep NO/manual-only and add end-to-end source/load mapping, insulation, heat, airflow and route-segment evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with full-route bend/clearance/strain, isolation and preserved post-action evidence; strengthen rail/load correlation and hidden-section coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates manual routing acceptance, tool-observable restoration and project-selected route coverage without inventing universal limits.

review_improvement: This review distinguishes Power Routing from the neighboring Power Connector row. The acceptance covers the entire energized harness path and its interaction with chassis thermal and mechanical features, not only connector seating.
independent_technical_reasoning: Power routing is a physical geometry and insulation test across a source-to-load path. Human inspection is required for abrasion, bend, heat exposure, airflow interference, strain and retention, so the complete case is MANUAL ONLY. Post-cycle telemetry can confirm that mapped loads returned, but cannot prove route safety. Project-specific drawings and energy controls are readiness requirements rather than BLOCKED conditions.

no_automatic_retry: On route damage, exposed conductor, heat/odor, unsafe interference, abnormal power/thermal evidence or load loss, preserve the route and raw state and stop. Do not reroute, reconnect again, energize, power-cycle or reset without an engineer-approved response.
